question: The total number of shared electrons in N₂ are ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The nitrogen molecule (N₂) consists of two nitrogen atoms connected by a triple bond.
 
• Each nitrogen atom has 5 valence electrons, making a total of 10 valence electrons for the N₂ molecule.
 
• In the triple bond, 6 electrons are shared between the two nitrogen atoms.
 
• This sharing of electrons results in a very strong bond, making N₂ a stable molecule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The triple bond in N₂ consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
 
• The triple bond contributes to the high bond dissociation energy of N₂, which is why nitrogen gas is relatively inert and does not react easily at room temperature.
 
• Nitrogen is essential for life and is a major component of amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
 
• Nitrogen fixation is the process by which nitrogen in the atmosphere is converted into ammonia or related nitrogenous compounds in soil.
